429	## D-020 — Inventory costing (moving average + FIFO layers, same-transaction COGS, no negative stock)
430	
431	**Decision.**
432	`inv_items.costing_method` enum MOVING_AVERAGE|FIFO, defaulted from item category, changeable only while no stock exists. Quantity SSOT remains `inv_stock_moves`.
433	
434	**Moving average:** `inv_item_valuations` (tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id, on_hand_qty QuantityType, avg_unit_cost full-precision, total_value MoneyType; UNIQUE(tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id)), updated in the SAME transaction as the move under `select(...).with_for_update()` — on Postgres this takes the row lock serializing concurrent movers; on SQLite the dialect silently OMITS the FOR UPDATE clause (it is a no-op, not an error — clarified from the drafts' contradictory claims), and SQLite's single-writer lock provides equivalent serialization; the PG locking path is proven by pg-marked concurrency tests in CI.
435	- Receipt: `total_value += receipt_value; on_hand_qty += qty; avg_unit_cost = total_value / on_hand_qty` unrounded.
436	- Issue: `cogs = quantize(qty × avg_unit_cost, currency dp, HALF_UP); total_value -= cogs`; when on_hand_qty hits 0, residual total_value is flushed to the price-difference account so value and quantity never disagree.
437	
438	**FIFO:** `inv_cost_layers` (id, tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id, receipt_move_id FK, received_at, original_qty, remaining_qty with CHECK `remaining_qty >= 0 AND remaining_qty <= original_qty`, unit_cost) plus `inv_layer_consumptions` (issue_move_id, layer_id, qty, cost). Issues consume layers ordered (received_at, id) ascending under `with_for_update`, one consumption row per touched layer; COGS = sum of per-layer quantized qty × unit_cost. Reversing an issue replays consumption rows backwards onto the exact layers; vendor returns consume layers normally; customer returns create a new layer at original COGS cost.
439	
440	**COGS consistency:** the in-process bus dispatches synchronously in the SAME session/transaction — inventory writes move + valuation/layer updates, publishes `inventory.stock.issued` carrying the computed cost and dimensions; `finance/handlers.py` posts the COGS journal entry (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory, dimensions copied: item, warehouse, cost center/WBS) before commit. One commit = move + valuation + journal + docflow link; a stock move can never exist without its journal entry or vice versa — explicitly recorded as the v1 decision whose future Kafka swap introduces a transactional outbox then, not now.
441	
442	**Negative stock forbidden outright:** service raises InsufficientStockError pre-flight, DB CHECKs (`on_hand_qty >= 0`, `remaining_qty >= 0`) back it; no per-warehouse opt-in. **Deadlock avoidance:** any transaction touching multiple valuation rows locks in (item_id, warehouse_id) sort order.
443	
444	**Rationale.**
445	The parity doc commits to moving average AND FIFO per item category with event-driven COGS posting. Same-transaction handling is the only design keeping stock value in the journal identical to the valuation table without reconciliation machinery, while the bus abstraction still decouples the modules at code level per CLAUDE.md rule 6. Layer consumption rows make COGS auditable per layer and reversals exact rather than recomputed. Banning negative stock makes FIFO well-defined and keeps the valuation CHECKs simple; shortage handling belongs to ATP/backorders per the parity doc.
446	
447	**Rejected alternatives.**
448	- Async/after-commit COGS: opens a stock-vs-GL divergence window requiring reconciliation jobs that contradict the universal-journal philosophy.
449	- Negative stock with provisional cost and retroactive correction (Odoo-style): requires retroactive revaluation clashing with posted-entry immutability.
450	- Global valuation row without warehouse dimension: parity scope is multi-warehouse and transfers need per-warehouse value.
451	- Report-time FIFO COGS recomputation: COGS must be a posted journal fact or statements change as layers mutate.
452	
453	**Risks & mitigations.**
454	- A finance handler bug rolls back inventory operations — intended (correctness over availability), documented for operators, tightly tested on the handler path.
455	- Moving-average rounding drift — absorbed by the zero-quantity flush rule, tested explicitly.
456	- SQLite cannot exercise true lock contention — accepted; the pg-marked tests carry that burden in CI.
457	
458	---
459	
460	## D-021 — Statements as pure projections + account-type model
461	
462	**Decision.**
463	`fin_accounts` (tenant_id, code, name, account_type ASSET|LIABILITY|EQUITY|REVENUE|EXPENSE, normal_balance derived from type, is_postable, cash_flow_category nullable OPERATING|INVESTING|FINANCING, is_cash_equivalent, account_group_id FK); `fin_account_groups` (tenant_id, code, name, parent_id self-FK, sort_order) as a pure presentation hierarchy; only leaf accounts postable.
464	
465	All statements build in `finance/service/statements.py` (reporting consumes via `finance/queries.py`) from ONE base aggregate over `fin_journal_lines` only — no header join, because lines denormalize tenant_id, posting_date, fiscal_period_id, is_posted (set during the posting transaction):
466	
467	```python
468	select(JournalLine.account_id,
469	       func.sum(functional_debit_amount - functional_credit_amount))
470	.where(tenant filter, is_posted == True, date predicates)
471	.group_by(account_id)
472	```
473	
474	MoneyType type propagation keeps sums exact on both backends.
475	
476	- **Trial balance** = that query split into per-account debit/credit totals.
477	- **P&L** = REVENUE+EXPENSE over a range.
478	- **Balance sheet** = ASSET/LIABILITY/EQUITY cumulative to a date, with retained earnings computed on the fly as cumulative REVENUE+EXPENSE net over ALL history to the as-of date, presented as a synthetic "Current and accumulated earnings" equity line (exact by construction, since v1 has no year-end carryforward per the parity doc).
479	- **Cash flow (indirect)** = net income + signed deltas of non-cash balance-sheet balances between two as-of dates grouped by cash_flow_category, with the service ASSERTING reconciliation to the movement on is_cash_equivalent accounts equals zero — a built-in self-check.
480	
481	**No stored totals anywhere:** no balance tables, no materialized views (CLAUDE.md rule 1).
482	
483	**Performance:** composite partial index `ix_fin_journal_lines_proj` ON (tenant_id, account_id, posting_date), declared with BOTH `postgresql_where=is_posted` AND `sqlite_where=is_posted` dialect kwargs (each engine needs its own — added; the draft named only one), plus `postgresql_include=['functional_debit_amount','functional_credit_amount']` for index-only scans on PG (kwarg harmlessly ignored on SQLite). Holds sub-second to ~10M lines on Postgres. Escape hatch if scale exceeds that: an explicitly-cache-semantics materialized view refreshed from the journal (journal stays SSOT), out of v1 and gated on a DECISIONS.md entry.
484	
485	The is_posted flag's agreement with header status is guaranteed by the two-flush posting protocol plus immutability triggers and asserted by a dedicated guard test.
486	
487	**Rationale.**
488	Direct implementation of the Universal Journal rule: views are projections, totals never stored, FI/CO reconciliation eliminated by construction. Five account types + cash_flow_category is the minimal metadata from which all four statements derive mechanically; computing retained earnings from full history is what makes "no carryforward in v1" sound rather than a correctness hole. One base query keeps every statement provably consistent with the trial balance — same predicate, same index.
489	
490	**Rejected alternatives.**
491	- Running-balance or period-totals tables updated on posting: violates CLAUDE.md rule 1 verbatim and reintroduces reconciliation.
492	- Account-code-range statement layout (classic SAP FSV intervals): the account_group FK hierarchy is simpler, referentially enforced, template-friendly.
493	- Direct cash-flow method: requires counterparty-cash tagging on every line; indirect derives from data already present.
494	- Materialized views in v1: premature and PG-only.
495	
496	**Risks & mitigations.**
497	- Cumulative-from-genesis balance-sheet queries grow linearly with history until balance carryforward ships (already a parity-doc "later") — the partial covering index keeps this an index-only scan on PG, and the carryforward job slots in later without schema change.
498	
499	---
500	
501	## D-022 — Alembic dual-database strategy and CI matrix
502	
503	**Decision.**
504	A single linear migration chain runs unmodified on both backends; migrations are the ONLY schema source — `Base.metadata.create_all` is banned everywhere INCLUDING tests, because triggers and raw DDL live only in migrations (tests would otherwise pass without the DB guards they claim to test). Rules:
505	
506	1. `env.py` uses the async pattern (`async_engine_from_config` + `connection.run_sync(do_run_migrations)`, `asyncio.run` in the offline-safe wrapper), reads `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL`, configures `compare_type=True` and `render_as_batch=True`.
507	2. Every ALTER goes through `with op.batch_alter_table(...)` unconditionally — pass-through on Postgres, copy-rebuild on SQLite — which requires deterministic constraint names: `core/models.py` declares `MetaData(naming_convention={'ix':'ix_%(column_0_label)s','uq':'uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s','ck':'ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s','fk':'fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s','pk':'pk_%(table_name)s'})`; unnamed constraints cannot be dropped in SQLite batch mode.
508	3. Type portability lives in the models (`with_variant` JSONB, `sa.Uuid`, MoneyType/QuantityType/RateType), so autogenerated revisions import those types from `app.core.models` and stay dialect-clean; hand review of every autogen revision is mandatory.
509	4. Trigger/function DDL: per-dialect string pairs side by side in the migration body under `if op.get_bind().dialect.name == 'postgresql': op.execute(PG_SQL) else: op.execute(SQLITE_SQL)`; stable names `trg_<table>_<purpose>`; upgrades DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS then CREATE; downgrades drop. **Rule (load-bearing):** any migration that batch-alters a trigger-bearing table MUST re-execute that table's trigger DDL afterwards, because SQLite's copy-rebuild silently drops triggers — recorded in the migration template comment and caught by the guard tests, which run against the final migrated schema. Postgres-only physical extras (GIN indexes, INCLUDE columns) sit in the same dialect branch with a plain-index or no-op SQLite arm.
510	5. CI, single `backend` job extended: **step A** `alembic upgrade head` + full `uv run pytest -q` on SQLite (file DB); **step B** `services: postgres:16` container — `alembic upgrade head`, then `alembic downgrade base && alembic upgrade head` (reversibility proof), then `uv run pytest -q -m pg` re-exercising the DB-guard subset (journal/period/audit triggers, JSONB paths, with_for_update contention, idempotency races) on real Postgres. The `pg` marker lives on `tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py`, period bypass tests, audit append-only tests, and inventory locking tests.
511	
512	**Rationale.**
513	D-003 fixed the dual-backend posture; this makes it mechanical. Batch-everywhere plus a naming convention is the canonical Alembic SQLite recipe; model-level type variance makes autogenerate output portable by construction; and running the financial-guard tests on real Postgres is what turns "enforced at DB level on BOTH" from an assertion into a tested claim. The trigger-recreation-after-batch rule prevents the silent-guard-loss failure mode that would otherwise pass every test until a rebuild migration ships.
514	
515	**Rejected alternatives.**
516	- Two migration branches per dialect: guaranteed drift, doubled review, breaks linear NNNN numbering.
517	- `create_all` for tests with a trigger fixture: duplicates trigger DDL outside migrations, violating single-source.
518	- Skipping Postgres in CI: trigger and FOR UPDATE behavior differ enough that untested-on-PG is unacceptable for the financial engine.
519	- Separate .sql files for trigger DDL: STRUCTURE forbids orphan files; migrations are self-contained.
520	
521	**Risks & mitigations.**
522	- Per-test isolation against the migrated schema is owned by D-025 (template-copy pattern) — the two decisions interlock and must not drift.
523	- Autogen occasionally emits dialect-specific DDL despite variants — mandatory hand review per STRUCTURE §8.6 plus the dual-engine CI run catches it.
524	
525	---
526	
527	## D-023 — Frontend type strategy (hand-written types.ts with compile-time drift gate)
528	
529	**Decision.**
530	Per STRUCTURE §4, each frontend module keeps a HAND-WRITTEN `src/modules/<module>/types.ts` mirroring that module's backend Pydantic Read/Create/Update/Filter schemas, snake_case preserved (no camelCase translation layer).
531	
532	**Mapping conventions, fixed:** Decimal/money → `string`; date/datetime → `string` (ISO 8601); UUID → `string`; backend enums → TS string-literal unions of the UPPER_SNAKE values (`type EntryStatus = 'DRAFT' | 'POSTED' | 'REVERSED'`); nullable/Optional → `| null`; Masked fields → `T | null`. Shared envelope types (`Page<T> {items, next_cursor, limit}`, `ApiError {error: {code, message, details, request_id}}`) live once in `src/lib/apiClient.ts`.
533	
534	**Drift control, two compile-time gates and zero runtime cost:**
535	
536	1. `backend/openapi.json` is COMMITTED and regenerated via a Makefile target (`make openapi` calls a tiny dump entry that instantiates the app factory and writes `app.openapi()`); a backend pytest test asserts the committed file equals the live app's schema, so any schema change that forgets regeneration fails the backend CI job with a "run make openapi" message.
537	2. A frontend devDependency `openapi-typescript` generates a GITIGNORED `src/lib/openapi.gen.d.ts` from `../backend/openapi.json` as a pre-step of `npm run typecheck`; each module adds a `types.contract.ts` containing only type-level assertions using Expect/Equal helpers from lib (`type _ = Expect<Equal<JournalEntry, components['schemas']['JournalEntryRead']>>`) — one line per mirrored type — so tsc fails on any divergence in either direction.
538	
539	Application code imports ONLY the hand-written `types.ts`; the generated file is referenced solely by contract files and is never committed (consistent with STRUCTURE §8.6: generated files are never hand-edited; here it is also never shipped). The CI frontend job's existing `npm run typecheck` therefore enforces the contract with no new job.
540	
541	**Rationale.**
542	STRUCTURE mandates hand-written mirrors, which keeps frontend types curated and readable — but hand-written without a gate guarantees drift. Routing the gate through the committed OpenAPI document gives an explicit, reviewable contract artifact whose own freshness is enforced backend-side, while the type-level Equal assertions catch field renames, nullability changes, and enum-value drift at compile time in both directions. String-typed money/dates align with the backend's Decimal-as-string serialization and force all formatting through `lib/format.ts` per STRUCTURE.
543	
544	**Rejected alternatives.**
545	- Fully generated committed types as the app's source: violates the hand-written mandate, bloats diffs, and produces unidiomatic deeply-nested component types.
546	- Runtime zod/valibot validation: a second schema source to keep in sync and runtime cost on every response; the API is first-party so compile-time checking suffices.
547	- No gate ("be careful"): drift is guaranteed across 13 modules.
548	- Comparing types via a custom AST script: reimplements what tsc's structural equality already does.
549	
550	**Risks & mitigations.**
551	- `openapi.json` merge conflicts on parallel schema work — resolved by regenerating (`make openapi`), never hand-merging.
552	- Contract files add one assertion line per type — trivial, and a missing assertion is visible in review because the convention is one contract file per module listed beside `types.ts`.
553	- `Equal<>` on very large unions can slow tsc marginally — bounded by module-scoped contract files.
554	
555	---
556	
557	## D-024 — Frontend auth: in-memory access token, cookie refresh, cross-tab single-flight
558	
559	**Decision.**
560	`src/lib/auth.ts` owns all token state. **Access token:** held ONLY in a module-scoped variable (with a subscribe hook for React state) — never localStorage/sessionStorage. **Refresh token:** never touched by JS (httpOnly cookie managed by the browser, scoped to `/api/v1/auth` per D-008). `apiClient.ts` attaches `Authorization: Bearer` from auth.ts on every call.
561	
562	- **Boot sequence:** app start calls `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` once (cookie present → new access+refresh pair, resumes the session silently; 401 → unauthenticated state, router redirects to /login).
563	- **Proactive renewal:** auth.ts decodes the access token's exp claim client-side (base64 decode only, no verification — it is not a trust decision) and schedules a refresh at exp minus 60 s.
564	- **Reactive path:** on any 401, apiClient triggers a single-flight refresh — within a tab, concurrent requests await one shared in-flight promise then retry exactly once; a second 401 after retry → hard logout.
565	- **Cross-tab coordination** (required because backend rotation invalidates the old refresh jti — even with the 10 s grace window, uncoordinated tabs hammering refresh is wrong): the refresher acquires `navigator.locks.request('atlas-auth-refresh')` so exactly one tab rotates, and broadcasts the new access token via `BroadcastChannel('atlas-auth')`; other tabs adopt it instead of refreshing; logout events broadcast the same way so all tabs clear state and redirect together.
566	- **Logout:** `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` (revokes the sid row, clears the cookie), clear memory, broadcast, `queryClient.clear()`.
567	- **Identity/permissions:** after any successful login/refresh-boot, fetch `GET /api/v1/auth/me` (user, tenant, permission keys) into TanStack Query; TanStack Router `beforeLoad` guards check auth.ts state and the permission set for route gating — UI-only convenience, the server remains the enforcement point.
568	- **Tenant selection** happens at login (tenant_slug field); the SPA never sends tenant headers — tenancy rides the JWT.
569	
570	**Rationale.**
571	Memory-only access tokens are XSS-resistant (no persistent readable storage) and the boot-refresh makes hard reloads seamless since the httpOnly cookie persists. Single-flight + Web Locks + BroadcastChannel is the standard answer to rotation-with-reuse-detection in multi-tab SPAs: it eliminates the benign-race family revocations the backend grace window only softens. Proactive renewal avoids latency spikes and thundering 401 retries. Keeping every fetch in apiClient.ts (per STRUCTURE) means the 401/retry/refresh logic exists exactly once.
572	
573	**Rejected alternatives.**
574	- localStorage/sessionStorage tokens: XSS-exfiltratable, explicitly rejected.
575	- Access token in a cookie too: makes every API call CSRF-relevant instead of just /auth.
576	- Per-tab independent refresh without coordination: races rotation and logs users out under normal multi-tab use.
577	- Service-worker token broker: strictly more moving parts for the same isolation in a v1 SPA.
578	- Storing permissions in localStorage for instant boot: stale-permission UI and another sync problem — /auth/me is one cheap request.
579	
580	**Risks & mitigations.**
581	- `navigator.locks`/BroadcastChannel need modern browsers — fine for v1 scope; a no-op fallback (per-tab single-flight only) keeps Safari/old engines working with the backend grace window absorbing the residual race.
582	- In-memory token dies on reload — by design; boot refresh restores it.
583	- Clock skew breaks proactive scheduling — harmless: the reactive 401 path is the safety net.
584	
585	---
586	
587	## D-025 — Backend testing strategy (async fixtures, per-test DB copies, trigger tests on SQLite)
588	
589	**Decision.**
590	pytest + pytest-asyncio with `asyncio_mode=auto`; HTTP tests use `httpx.AsyncClient` over `ASGITransport(app)` — no live server.
591	
592	**Database isolation uses the TEMPLATE-COPY pattern**, deliberately replacing the draft's SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction approach, which breaks the moment code under test performs REAL commits — and ours does by design (idempotency's separate reservation transaction, `run_in_uow` commits, numbering claims): a session-scoped fixture builds ONE migrated template SQLite file via programmatic `alembic.command.upgrade(config, 'head')` (env.py's `asyncio.run` pattern works because the session fixture runs outside any event loop); a function-scoped fixture copies that file (`shutil.copy`, ~ms) into tmp_path, builds an aiosqlite engine on the copy with the connect-event `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, and overrides the app's session dependency. Every test gets a fully migrated, trigger-bearing, fresh database where real commits are allowed and nothing leaks across tests. For the pg-marked subset in CI, a fixture creates a per-test database via `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE atlas_test_template` from a once-migrated template database and drops it after — same semantics on Postgres.
593	
594	**Fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`:** `tenant_factory` provisions tenant + admin user + role with named permissions through the REAL provisioning service under `system_context`, returning a handle with tenant_id and an `auth_headers(user)` helper that performs a real login; `authed_client` composes it; `permissions_context` sets the `current_permissions` ContextVar for serializer-level masking tests; module fixtures live in `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` per STRUCTURE §6.
595	
596	**DB-guard tests** (`tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py` etc.) deliberately use raw `session.execute(text(...))` to BYPASS the service layer — sanctioned because the CI grep gate banning `text()` is scoped to `app/`, not `tests/` — asserting that UPDATE/DELETE on posted lines, unbalanced DRAFT→POSTED, closed-period posting, and audit UPDATE/DELETE all raise with the `ATLAS_` tokens on SQLite, with the same tests re-run on Postgres via `-m pg`. The tenancy suite enumerates `Base.registry.mappers` (auto-covering new models); event-bus tests assert handler effects and rollback-on-handler-failure within one transaction; idempotency tests exercise the two-transaction reservation flow with real commits; determinism comes from explicit posting_date/anchor arguments in factories, not clock freezing.
597	
598	**Rationale.**
599	The template-copy pattern is the single decision that makes everything else testable as designed: SAVEPOINT isolation silently converts the idempotency guard's real COMMIT into a savepoint release (changing the very semantics under test) and shares state when code opens a second session. File copies are milliseconds on SQLite and CREATE DATABASE TEMPLATE is fast on Postgres, so the cost is negligible while every test sees the exact schema migrations produce — triggers included, which is the whole point of asserting DB guards in CI. Factories going through real services means tenancy stamping, numbering, docflow, and audit are exercised by every test that touches data.
600	
601	**Rejected alternatives.**
602	- SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction per test (the draft): incompatible with real multi-transaction code paths and second sessions; rejected as the primary pattern.
603	- `create_all` + trigger fixture: duplicates DDL outside migrations and tests a schema nobody ships.
604	- In-memory `:memory:` SQLite: cannot be shared across connections/sessions the way the app's engine needs, and cannot be template-copied.
605	- One shared DB with truncation between tests: ordering-sensitive and slow on Postgres.
606	
607	**Risks & mitigations.**
608	- Session-scoped template means schema changes require fixture cache invalidation — the template path embeds the Alembic head revision in its filename, so a new revision automatically rebuilds.
609	- Per-test PG database creation is slower (~100 ms each) — confined to the small pg-marked subset.
610	- Raw-SQL bypass tests are tightly coupled to trigger names/tokens — intentional pinning; they exist to fail when guards change.
611	
612	---
613	
614	## D-026 — Seed-data architecture (deterministic, per-template, three months of linked transactions)
615	
616	**Decision.**
617	`backend/seed.py` is a CLI (argparse: `--templates` defaulting to all five industry templates, `--anchor-date` defaulting to today, `--reset`) that assumes a migrated database (Makefile target chains `alembic upgrade head`).
618	
619	**Determinism:** one `random.Random(f'{template}:{anchor_date}')` per tenant — identical output for a given (template, anchor) pair; the anchor is recorded on the tenant so reruns are reproducible for bug reports.
620	
621	**Provisioning phase** under `system_context()`: per template, create tenant (slug `demo-<template>`, fixed admin credentials sourced from `.env.example` values), apply the YAML industry template via the industry module's real application service — modules toggled, display labels, chart-of-accounts preset, tax codes, number-sequence patterns, system roles, custom-field defs (written through `core/custom_fields.py`).
622	
623	**Transaction phase:** set the tenancy ContextVar to the tenant (NOT `system_context` — business writes must be stamped and filtered normally) and drive everything through the REAL service layer wrapped in `run_in_uow()`, never raw inserts — so numbering, docflow registration and links, domain events (goods issue → COGS), audit rows, and DB triggers all fire exactly as in production, making seed a standing integration proof.
624	
625	**Script per template spans 3 calendar months ending at anchor:** master data first (items, vendors, customers, warehouses, employees, WBS elements, exchange rates including one foreign currency); then interlinked flows — procurement P2P chains (requisition → PO → goods receipt → AP invoice → payment run), sales O2C (quote → order → delivery → customer invoice → receipt, including partial shipments and one open backorder), template-specific depth (production orders with WIP postings for manufacturing; projects + timesheets for professional-services; maintenance orders for construction; quality inspection lots for healthcare/retail receiving), foreign-currency invoices plus a month-end FX revaluation run, manual journal entries, and month-end closes: periods for months 1 and 2 CLOSED via the real period-close service, month 3 left OPEN with open AP/AR items so aging, dunning, and dashboards have live data. Volumes ~100-300 documents per tenant (seconds on SQLite).
626	
627	**Idempotency:** without `--reset`, seed refuses if a demo tenant exists; `--reset` hard-deletes the demo tenants by cascade — the ONLY sanctioned hard-delete path in the codebase, running under `system_context` and documented as such.
628	
629	**Self-verification:** seed ends by asserting, per tenant, (a) trial balance debits == credits, (b) every created document's docflow chain traverses end-to-end, (c) inventory GL balance == sum of `inv_item_valuations` — and CI runs seed against SQLite after the test suite as a smoke gate.
630	
631	**Rationale.**
632	Seeding through real services is the load-bearing choice: SQL-dump seeds rot with every migration and bypass exactly the invariants (gapless numbers, docflow, COGS events, period triggers) the demo exists to showcase, while service-driven seeding doubles as an end-to-end integration test the CI runs for free. Deterministic RNG + recorded anchor gives reproducible demos and bug reports without freezing real time. Closing two of three months demonstrates the period-close machinery and leaves believable open items for the operational screens.
633	
634	**Rejected alternatives.**
635	- SQL dump / fixtures files: bypass invariants, drift with schema, undebuggable diffs.
636	- Faker with random seed-per-run: non-reproducible demo states.
637	- Seeding via HTTP API: needs a running server and auth choreography for zero added fidelity — the service layer is the contract.
638	- A full year of data: slower seeds for no demo value; the parity scope's reports all read well at 3 months.
639	
640	**Risks & mitigations.**
641	- Anchor defaulting to today means runs on different days differ in dates (structure stays identical given anchor) — acceptable; CI pins a fixed anchor for the smoke gate.
642	- Seed duration creeps as modules land — bounded by per-tenant volume caps and the CI timing check.
643	- The `--reset` cascade is a footgun if pointed at a non-demo tenant — guarded by a slug prefix check (refuses anything not starting with `demo-`).

1	"""Purchase orders (PLAN 6.2): the ``PurchaseOrder`` header + ``PurchaseOrderLine``.
2	
3	A PO is the committing P2P document — the vendor commitment. The header mixes in ``DocumentMixin``
4	and carries a gapless ``po_number`` claimed at creation (D-040). It may be raised FROM an approved
5	requisition AND/OR a quoted RFQ (``source_requisition_id`` / ``source_rfq_id`` — nullable composite
6	tenant FKs + docflow edges). ``payment_terms_days`` is SNAPSHOT from the vendor at creation (so a
7	later vendor edit cannot rewrite an open PO's terms — the AP bill in 6.4 reads the snapshot).
8	``total_amount`` is the maintained sum of line nets. ``approved_by`` / ``approved_at`` record who
9	cleared the approval gate.
10	
11	Each line carries an OPAQUE inventory ``item_id`` / ``uom_id`` (D-029), the negotiated
12	``unit_cost``,
13	the derived ``line_amount`` (qty × unit_cost), ``received_quantity`` (default 0 — updated by 6.3
14	goods receipts; the column lands now so the open-quantity query + 6.3 GR need no migration), and an
15	opaque finance ``tax_code_id`` (nullable — the bill in 6.4 uses it). Money/quantity use
16	``MoneyType`` / ``QuantityType`` (D-015). PERFORMANCE §1 indexes: (tenant, status) and
17	(tenant, vendor_id, status).
18	"""
19	
20	import uuid
21	from datetime import date, datetime
22	
23	import sqlalchemy as sa
24	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
25	
26	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
27	from app.core.models import (
28	    AuditMixin,
29	    Base,
30	    TenantMixin,
31	    TimestampMixin,
32	    UuidPKMixin,
33	    tenant_fk,
34	    tenant_unique,
35	)
36	from app.core.money import MoneyType, QuantityType
37	from app.modules.procurement.constants import PurchaseOrderStatus
38	
39	
40	class PurchaseOrder(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
41	    """A purchase order header (PLAN 6.2). ``po_number`` is claimed at creation (D-040).
42	    ``vendor_id`` is a composite tenant FK to proc_vendors (validated ACTIVE at create). ``status``
43	    runs the PurchaseOrderStatus lifecycle; the SEND step evaluates the PURCHASE_ORDER approval
44	    threshold on ``total_amount`` (≥ threshold ⇒ PENDING_APPROVAL, below ⇒ auto APPROVED).
45	    ``payment_terms_days`` is snapshot from the vendor at create. ``source_requisition_id`` /
46	    ``source_rfq_id`` are nullable composite tenant FKs to the documents this PO was converted from.
47	    Audited (D-010)."""
48	
49	    __tablename__ = "proc_purchase_orders"
50	    __table_args__ = (
51	        tenant_unique(),
52	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
53	        document_fk(),
54	        tenant_fk("proc_vendors", "vendor_id"),
55	        tenant_fk("proc_requisitions", "source_requisition_id"),
56	        tenant_fk("proc_rfqs", "source_rfq_id"),
57	        # PERFORMANCE §1: the PO list filters on (tenant, status) and a vendor's POs by status.
58	        sa.Index("ix_proc_purchase_orders_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"),
59	        sa.Index(
60	            "ix_proc_purchase_orders_tenant_id_vendor_id_status",
61	            "tenant_id",
62	            "vendor_id",
63	            "status",
64	        ),
65	    )
66	
67	    po_number: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
68	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
69	        sa.String(20),
70	        nullable=False,
71	        default=PurchaseOrderStatus.DRAFT.value,
72	        server_default="DRAFT",
73	    )
74	    vendor_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
75	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
76	    order_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
77	    expected_date: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=True)
78	    # Net-days terms snapshot from the vendor at create (the AP bill in 6.4 reads this snapshot so a
79	    # later vendor edit cannot rewrite an open PO's due-date math).
80	    payment_terms_days: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
81	    total_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
82	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
83	    )
84	    notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)
85	    # Approval audit: who cleared the gate and when (NULL until approved).
86	    approved_by: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
87	    approved_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
88	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True
89	    )
90	    source_requisition_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
91	    source_rfq_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)

3	
4	Started as a SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line
5	cap, the finance precedent); PLAN 6.1+6.2 still sit under that.
6	
7	PLAN 6.2 adds the requisition → RFQ → PO document chain and the data-driven approval-threshold
8	rule. The three documents carry gapless numbers claimed AT CREATION (D-040: a procurement document
9	is referenceable the moment it exists — a DRAFT requisition already prints a PR number that the
10	sourcing/ordering chain quotes — unlike finance, which numbers at posting; gaplessness still holds
11	because creation is the committing transaction). The approval rule is a single-characteristic
12	(amount) value-threshold rule per the s4hana-parity Procurement section (multi-characteristic /
13	multi-step release strategies are the documented later).
14	
15	**Payment-terms modeling (decided here).** A vendor carries ``payment_terms_days`` — a plain
16	integer net-days value (30 = NET30) — NOT a separate terms master/value-set. This matches how AP
17	already computes a bill's due date (bill_date + net days) and keeps v1 simple; richer term
18	schedules (e.g. 2/10 NET30 early-payment discounts, multi-instalment plans) are deferred per the
19	parity doc and would arrive as a terms entity referenced from the vendor. The field is stored with
20	a CHECK >= 0 on the vendor.
21	
22	**Vendor codes are USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant** (the ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, vendor_code)`` on
23	proc_vendors) — mirroring inventory ``item_code`` and the finance account ``code``: a vendor MASTER
24	carries no gapless document number (a code, not a number). The P2P DOCUMENTS in 6.2+ (requisitions,
25	POs, GRs) DO claim gapless numbers — a posted document in the D-012 sense — but the master does not.
26	"""

38	      chain (6.2) refuses to raise a NEW PO against it (a soft block; the vendor can be unblocked
39	      back to ACTIVE).

129	class GoodsReceiptStatus(StrEnum):

152	class MatchStatus(StrEnum):
153	    """Lifecycle of a 3-way invoice match — the procure-to-pay closing document (PLAN 6.4, D-042).

155	    A match compares a vendor's invoice against the PO (price) and the goods receipt (quantity);

4	from-scratch and convert paths produce identical PO rows.

6	Lifecycle (constants.PurchaseOrderStatus) — states SET in 6.2: DRAFT → (send) PENDING_APPROVAL or
7	APPROVED → SENT, plus REJECTED / CANCELLED. PARTIALLY_RECEIVED / RECEIVED / CLOSED are driven by 6.3
8	goods receipts (declared in constants, transitions land later).

11	and EVERY line item must be in the vendor's approved-items list (else 422
12	procurement.item_not_approved). ``line_amount`` = qty × unit_cost; ``total_amount`` = Σ line_amount;

252	    threshold on total_amount: ≥ threshold ⇒ PENDING_APPROVAL (an approver must clear it before it
253	    can be sent); below ⇒ auto APPROVED then SENT. An already-APPROVED PO is sent directly. A
254	    PENDING_APPROVAL / REJECTED / SENT+ PO cannot be (re-)sent here."""
255	    po = await get_purchase_order(session, tenant_id, po_id)
256	    status = PurchaseOrderStatus(po.status)

259	        needs_approval = await approvals.requires_approval(
260	            session,

270	                session, tenant_id, po.document_id, status=po.status
271	            )
272	            return po

274	        po.status = PurchaseOrderStatus.SENT.value

276	        await session.flush()

3	Each conversion copies the predecessor's lines into the successor, links the two registry entries
4	with a docflow edge (the D-012 chain the DocFlowViewer renders), sets the successor's ``source_*``
5	id, and advances the predecessor's status (a converted requisition → CONVERTED; a quoted RFQ that
6	becomes a PO → CLOSED). The successor is created through the from-scratch writers in ``rfqs`` /
7	``orders`` so it goes through the SAME validation + numbering + document registration (no second
8	code path). Idempotency (D-013) is owned by the endpoints.

80	    rfq = await rfqs.create_rfq(
81	        session,
82	        tenant_id,
83	        RfqCreate(
84	            vendor_id=payload.vendor_id,
85	            currency_code=currency,
86	            valid_until=payload.valid_until,
87	            notes=payload.notes,
88	            lines=[
89	                RfqLineCreate(
90	                    item_id=line.item_id,
91	                    description=line.description,
92	                    quantity=Decimal(str(line.quantity)),
93	                    uom_id=line.uom_id,
94	                )
95	                for line in req_lines
96	            ],
97	        ),
98	    )
99	    rfq.source_requisition_id = requisition_id
100	    await session.flush()
101	    await docflow.link_documents(
102	        session,
103	        tenant_id,
104	        predecessor=req.document_id,
105	        successor=rfq.document_id,
106	        link_type=REQUISITION_SOURCED_BY_RFQ_LINK,
107	    )
108	    req.status = RequisitionStatus.CONVERTED.value
109	    await session.flush()
110	    await docflow.set_document_status(
111	        session, tenant_id, req.document_id, status=RequisitionStatus.CONVERTED.value
112	    )
113	    return rfq

116	async def convert_requisition_to_po(
117	    session: AsyncSession,
118	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
119	    requisition_id: uuid.UUID,
120	    payload: PurchaseOrderFromRequisition,
121	) -> PurchaseOrder:
122	    """Order an APPROVED requisition straight into a PO (PLAN 6.2): copy lines with unit_cost from
123	    the requisition estimate, snapshot the vendor's terms/currency, write the PO (which enforces the
124	    vendor-ACTIVE + approved-items rules), link docflow requisition→po ('ordered_by'), set
125	    source_requisition_id, and mark the requisition CONVERTED. A line without an estimated cost is
126	    rejected (a PO line needs a price)."""
127	    req = await _require_approved_requisition(session, tenant_id, requisition_id)
128	    req_lines = await requisitions.get_requisition_lines(session, tenant_id, requisition_id)
129	    await require_active_vendor(session, tenant_id, payload.vendor_id)
130	    currency, terms = await orders._resolve_header_defaults(
131	        session, tenant_id, payload.vendor_id, None
132	    )
133	
134	    po_lines: list[_PoLineInput] = []
135	    for line in req_lines:
136	        if line.estimated_unit_cost is None:
137	            raise ValidationFailedError(
138	                message="A requisition line has no estimated cost; a PO line needs a price",
139	                code="procurement.requisition_line_no_estimate",
140	                details={"item_id": str(line.item_id)},
141	            )
142	        po_lines.append(
143	            _PoLineInput(
144	                item_id=line.item_id,
145	                description=line.description,
146	                quantity=Decimal(str(line.quantity)),
147	                uom_id=line.uom_id,
148	                unit_cost=Decimal(str(line.estimated_unit_cost)),
149	                tax_code_id=None,
150	            )
151	        )
152	    po = await write_purchase_order(
153	        session,
154	        tenant_id,
155	        vendor_id=payload.vendor_id,
156	        currency_code=currency,
157	        payment_terms_days=terms,
158	        order_date=payload.order_date or date.today(),
159	        expected_date=payload.expected_date,
160	        notes=payload.notes,
161	        lines=po_lines,
162	        source_requisition_id=requisition_id,
163	    )
164	    await docflow.link_documents(
165	        session,
166	        tenant_id,
167	        predecessor=req.document_id,
168	        successor=po.document_id,
169	        link_type=REQUISITION_ORDERED_BY_PO_LINK,
170	    )
171	    req.status = RequisitionStatus.CONVERTED.value
172	    await session.flush()
173	    await docflow.set_document_status(
174	        session, tenant_id, req.document_id, status=RequisitionStatus.CONVERTED.value
175	    )
176	    return po
177	
178	
179	async def convert_rfq_to_po(
180	    session: AsyncSession,
181	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
182	    rfq_id: uuid.UUID,
183	    payload: PurchaseOrderFromRfq,
184	) -> PurchaseOrder:
185	    """Order a QUOTED RFQ into a PO (PLAN 6.2): copy lines with unit_cost from the RFQ's quoted
186	    prices, take the vendor + currency from the RFQ, snapshot the vendor's terms, write the PO, link
187	    docflow rfq→po ('ordered_by'), set source_rfq_id, and CLOSE the RFQ. A line without a quote is
188	    rejected."""
189	    rfq = await rfqs.get_rfq(session, tenant_id, rfq_id)
190	    if RfqStatus(rfq.status) != RfqStatus.QUOTED:
191	        raise ConflictError(
192	            message="Only a quoted RFQ can be converted to a purchase order",
193	            code="procurement.rfq_not_quoted",
194	            details={"status": rfq.status},
195	        )
196	    await require_active_vendor(session, tenant_id, rfq.vendor_id)
197	    rfq_lines = await rfqs.get_rfq_lines(session, tenant_id, rfq_id)
198	    _, terms = await orders._resolve_header_defaults(session, tenant_id, rfq.vendor_id, None)
199	
200	    po_lines: list[_PoLineInput] = []
201	    for line in rfq_lines:
202	        if line.quoted_unit_cost is None:
203	            raise ValidationFailedError(
204	                message="An RFQ line has no quoted cost; a PO line needs a price",
205	                code="procurement.rfq_line_no_quote",
206	                details={"item_id": str(line.item_id)},
207	            )
208	        po_lines.append(
209	            _PoLineInput(
210	                item_id=line.item_id,
211	                description=line.description,
212	                quantity=Decimal(str(line.quantity)),
213	                uom_id=line.uom_id,
214	                unit_cost=Decimal(str(line.quoted_unit_cost)),
215	                tax_code_id=None,
216	            )
217	        )
218	    po = await write_purchase_order(
219	        session,
220	        tenant_id,
221	        vendor_id=rfq.vendor_id,
222	        currency_code=rfq.currency_code,
223	        payment_terms_days=terms,
224	        order_date=payload.order_date or date.today(),
225	        expected_date=payload.expected_date,
226	        notes=payload.notes,
227	        lines=po_lines,
228	        source_rfq_id=rfq_id,
229	    )
230	    await docflow.link_documents(
231	        session,
232	        tenant_id,
233	        predecessor=rfq.document_id,
234	        successor=po.document_id,
235	        link_type=RFQ_ORDERED_BY_PO_LINK,
236	    )
237	    rfq.status = RfqStatus.CLOSED.value
238	    await session.flush()
239	    await docflow.set_document_status(
240	        session, tenant_id, rfq.document_id, status=RfqStatus.CLOSED.value
241	    )
242	    return po

1	"""Shared validation + numbering helpers for the P2P document services (PLAN 6.2).
2	
3	Kept in one private module so the requisition / RFQ / PO services stay small and the cross-module
4	validation rules (item exists, currency exists, vendor ACTIVE, item approved for vendor) live in ONE
5	place — greppable and consistent. Every check goes through the owning module's queries contract
6	(D-029), never a cross-module FK. The numbering helper wraps ensure_sequence + claim_number so the
7	three documents claim their gapless number at creation identically (D-040).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	from datetime import date
14	from decimal import Decimal
15	
16	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
17	
18	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
19	from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
20	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
21	from app.modules.inventory import queries as inventory_queries
22	from app.modules.procurement import queries as procurement_queries
23	from app.modules.procurement.constants import VendorStatus
24	
25	
26	async def validate_currency(
27	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, currency_code: str
28	) -> None:
29	    """The currency must exist in finance's catalog (D-029, via finance/queries)."""
30	    if not await finance_queries.currency_exists(session, tenant_id, currency_code):
31	        raise ValidationFailedError(
32	            message=f"Currency {currency_code} does not exist in the finance catalog",
33	            code="procurement.currency_not_found",
34	            details={"currency_code": currency_code},
35	        )
36	
37	
38	async def validate_item(
39	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
40	) -> None:
41	    """The item must exist in inventory (D-029, via inventory/queries.item_exists)."""
42	    if not await inventory_queries.item_exists(session, tenant_id, item_id):
43	        raise ValidationFailedError(
44	            message="Referenced inventory item does not exist",
45	            code="procurement.item_not_found",
46	            details={"item_id": str(item_id)},
47	        )
48	
49	
50	def validate_quantity(quantity: Decimal) -> Decimal:
51	    """A document line quantity must be > 0 (every requisition/RFQ/PO line)."""
52	    qty = Decimal(str(quantity))
53	    if qty <= 0:
54	        raise ValidationFailedError(
55	            message="A line quantity must be greater than zero",
56	            code="procurement.line_quantity_invalid",
57	            details={"quantity": str(qty)},
58	        )
59	    return qty
60	
61	
62	async def require_active_vendor(
63	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, vendor_id: uuid.UUID
64	) -> None:
65	    """The vendor must exist AND be ACTIVE (not BLOCKED/INACTIVE) — the v1 PO source-control rule.
66	    Reads the vendor's status via procurement/queries (intra-module). A BLOCKED/INACTIVE vendor
67	    cannot receive a NEW PO (constants.VendorStatus documents the soft block)."""
68	    vendor = await procurement_queries.get_vendor(session, tenant_id, vendor_id)
69	    if vendor is None:
70	        raise ValidationFailedError(
71	            message="Referenced vendor does not exist",
72	            code="procurement.vendor_not_found",
73	            details={"vendor_id": str(vendor_id)},
74	        )
75	    if VendorStatus(vendor.status) != VendorStatus.ACTIVE:
76	        raise ValidationFailedError(
77	            message=f"Vendor is {vendor.status}; a purchase order needs an ACTIVE vendor",
78	            code="procurement.vendor_not_active",
79	            details={"vendor_id": str(vendor_id), "status": vendor.status},
80	        )
81	
82	
83	async def require_item_approved_for_vendor(
84	    session: AsyncSession,
85	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
86	    vendor_id: uuid.UUID,
87	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
88	) -> None:
89	    """A PO line item MUST be in the vendor's approved-items list — the v1 source-control rule
90	    (D-040: enforce approved sources). Reads via procurement/queries.is_item_approved_for_vendor (an
91	    inactive approval counts as not approved). Raises 422 procurement.item_not_approved
92	    otherwise."""
93	    if not await procurement_queries.is_item_approved_for_vendor(
94	        session, tenant_id, vendor_id, item_id
95	    ):
96	        raise ValidationFailedError(
97	            message="The item is not an approved source for this vendor",
98	            code="procurement.item_not_approved",
99	            details={"vendor_id": str(vendor_id), "item_id": str(item_id)},
100	        )
101	
102	
103	async def claim_document_number(
104	    session: AsyncSession,
105	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
106	    *,
107	    sequence_name: str,
108	    prefix: str,
109	    padding: int,
110	    on_date: date,
111	) -> str:
112	    """Ensure the sequence exists (year-resetting) and claim the next gapless number (D-040: claimed
113	    at creation, so a document is referenceable immediately). The claim runs in the caller's
114	    transaction so gaplessness for committed documents falls out of ACID."""
115	    await ensure_sequence(session, tenant_id, sequence_name, prefix, padding, year_reset=True)
116	    return await claim_number(session, tenant_id, sequence_name, on_date=on_date)
117

1	"""Sales constants (STRUCTURE §3): the customer-master + pricing enums, the pricing-engine defaults,
2	and the permission keys, registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).
3	
4	A SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line cap, the
5	finance precedent); PLAN 7.1's customer master + condition-style pricing sit under that. The
6	order/delivery/invoice document chain (7.2–7.4) will add its own status enums, document types and
7	number sequences here as it lands.
8	
9	**Customer codes are USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant** (the ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, customer_code)``
10	on sales_customers) — mirroring the procurement ``vendor_code`` and inventory ``item_code``: a
11	customer MASTER carries no gapless document number (a code, not a number). The SALES DOCUMENTS in
12	7.2+ (quotes, orders, deliveries, invoices) DO claim gapless numbers — a posted document in the
13	D-012 sense — but the master does not.
14	
15	**Credit-limit semantics (decided here, D-043).** ``Customer.credit_limit`` is a non-null
16	``MoneyType`` defaulting to 0 and meaning the maximum outstanding AR (open invoices) the customer
17	may carry. It is interpreted as:
18	
19	- ``0`` (the default) → CASH-ONLY: the customer is allowed no open credit at all, so 7.2's order
20	  confirmation blocks if confirming would leave ANY positive outstanding AR. New customers are
21	  cash-only until a limit is set explicitly.
22	- a positive value → the credit ceiling: 7.2 blocks confirmation when outstanding AR + the new
23	  order would exceed it.
24	
25	There is deliberately NO "unlimited" sentinel in v1 (a NULL credit_limit is NOT used): "unlimited"
26	is expressed by setting a very large explicit limit, keeping the column non-null and the 7.2 check a
27	single unconditional comparison with no NULL branch. This is the static credit-limit block the
28	s4hana-parity Sales section scopes to v1 (no exposure aggregation across open orders/deliveries, no
29	finance-owned exposure ledger — documented there as a later).
30	
31	**Customer group (decided here).** A customer optionally belongs to ONE ``CustomerGroup`` — a lean
32	``sales_customer_groups`` (tenant, code, name) MASTER table, NOT a free-string column. A master
33	table is chosen because pricing keys on the group: a ``PriceList`` targets a group by id (a
34	composite tenant FK), so both the customer and the price list reference the same group rows, the
35	group's name is editable in one place, and a typo'd free-string group can never silently exclude a
36	customer from its price list. The group carries NO pricing of its own — it is purely a grouping key.
37	"""
38	
39	from enum import StrEnum
40	
41	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions
42	
43	
44	class CustomerStatus(StrEnum):
45	    """A customer's lifecycle / usability state (parity: customer master block levels).
46	
47	    - ACTIVE: usable — new quotes/orders may name this customer (the only state 7.2+ accepts).
48	    - BLOCKED: temporarily barred — kept for history and existing open documents, but the O2C chain
49	      (7.2) refuses to confirm a NEW order against it (a soft block, distinct from the credit-limit
50	      block; the customer can be unblocked back to ACTIVE).
51	    - INACTIVE: retired — no new business, retained for reporting and existing AR history.
52	
53	    Transitions are unrestricted between the three (ACTIVE↔BLOCKED↔INACTIVE all allowed): a block is
54	    reversible and a retired customer can be reactivated. The only rule the service enforces is that
55	    the target is a valid CustomerStatus; no terminal state, because customer history must stay
56	    referenceable and a mistaken retire/block must be undoable (the append-only ledger lives in
57	    finance AR, not here) — the procurement VendorStatus precedent."""
58	
59	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
60	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
61	    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"
62	
63	
64	class PriceListStatus(StrEnum):
65	    """A price list's usability state. Only ACTIVE lists are considered by the price resolver; an
66	    INACTIVE list is retained (history, a seasonal list parked between campaigns) but never priced
67	    from. Transitions are unrestricted between the two (a list can be re-activated)."""
68	
69	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
70	    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"
71	
72	
73	class DiscountType(StrEnum):
74	    """How a per-order-LINE discount is expressed (PLAN 7.2 applies it; defined here so the wire
75	    contract is stable from the start, the MatchStatus-declared-early precedent).
76	
77	    - PERCENT: a percentage off the resolved base price (e.g. 10 = 10% off).
78	    - AMOUNT: an absolute amount off per unit in the line's currency.
79	
80	    The PRICE LIST itself carries no discount — it yields the base unit price only (the condition
81	    base). Discounts are an order-line concern (7.2), so the resolver in 7.1 returns the base price
82	    untouched; this enum is the vocabulary those lines will use."""
83	
84	    PERCENT = "PERCENT"
85	    AMOUNT = "AMOUNT"
86	
87	
88	# The default net-days a customer is created with when the payload omits it (NET30 — the common
89	# commercial default; AR's due-date math is invoice_date + this many days). Stored on the customer
90	# with a CHECK >= 0; mirrors the procurement vendor payment-terms model.
91	DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30
92	
93	# A customer's credit_limit defaults to 0 = CASH-ONLY (D-043, documented in the module docstring):
94	# no open credit allowed. Stored on the customer as a non-null MoneyType with a CHECK >= 0.
95	DEFAULT_CREDIT_LIMIT = 0
96	
97	# A new price list's default priority. When several ACTIVE lists match the same item/customer/date/
98	# currency/quantity, the resolver picks the HIGHEST priority first (D-043 resolution order); equal
99	# priorities fall through to specificity (group-targeted beats general) then latest valid_from. A
100	# higher integer = higher priority. The default 0 means "no explicit priority"; a tenant raises a
101	# list's priority to make it win ties. Stored with a CHECK >= 0.
102	DEFAULT_PRICE_LIST_PRIORITY = 0
103	
104	
105	# --- Permissions (D-009): one key per guarded endpoint action -----------------
106	# Customer master (PLAN 7.1): read the customer master (+ customer groups) vs create/edit it.
107	# Customer-group management rides CUSTOMER_MANAGE (the inventory item/uom-conversion precedent:
108	# closely-related master config shares the parent entity's manage key — a group is a customer
109	# grouping, managed by whoever manages customers).
110	SALES_CUSTOMER_READ = "sales.customer.read"
111	SALES_CUSTOMER_MANAGE = "sales.customer.manage"
112	# Price lists (PLAN 7.1): read the price lists (+ their items, + a resolved price quote) vs
113	# create/edit them (and their items). Pricing is a distinct authority from the customer master.
114	SALES_PRICELIST_READ = "sales.pricelist.read"
115	SALES_PRICELIST_MANAGE = "sales.pricelist.manage"
116	
117	register_permissions(
118	    SALES_CUSTOMER_READ,
119	    SALES_CUSTOMER_MANAGE,
120	    SALES_PRICELIST_READ,
121	    SALES_PRICELIST_MANAGE,
122	    descriptions={
123	        SALES_CUSTOMER_READ: "Read customers and customer groups",
124	        SALES_CUSTOMER_MANAGE: "Create and edit customers and customer groups",
125	        SALES_PRICELIST_READ: "Read price lists, their items and resolved price quotes",
126	        SALES_PRICELIST_MANAGE: "Create and edit price lists and their items",
127	    },
128	)
129

1	"""Sales customer master (PLAN 7.1): the ``CustomerGroup`` grouping master and the ``Customer``
2	entity — near-symmetric with the procurement vendor master.
3	
4	First file in the sales ``models/`` package (STRUCTURE §3: a models/ package from the start because
5	customers + pricing together exceed the 400-line cap, the finance/inventory/procurement precedent).
6	Re-exported from ``models/__init__`` so ``from app.modules.sales.models import Customer`` works from
7	one surface.
8	
9	Design decisions baked in here:
10	
11	- **The customer's id IS finance AR's opaque ``partner_id`` (D-029).** Finance owns no customer
12	  table; every AR invoice/receipt carries an opaque ``partner_id`` (no FK) + a denormalized
13	  ``partner_name``. That id is exactly this ``Customer.id``. Sales is ABOVE finance in the
14	  dependency order, so finance can never FK to this table; the link is by opaque id only, resolved
15	  through ``sales/queries.get_customer_for_partner`` — the exact mirror of the vendor↔partner_id
16	  link.
17	
18	- **``credit_limit`` is a non-null ``MoneyType`` (D-043).** It is the maximum outstanding AR the
19	  customer may carry: 0 (the default) = cash-only (no open credit), a positive value = the ceiling.
20	  No NULL/unlimited sentinel (constants.py documents why). A DB CHECK keeps it >= 0; 7.2's order
21	  confirmation reads it for the static credit-limit block.
22	
23	- **``payment_terms_days`` is a plain net-days integer** (30 = NET30) driving AR due dates
24	  (invoice_date + days), the vendor precedent; a DB CHECK keeps it >= 0.
25	
26	- **``customer_group_id`` is an intra-module composite ``tenant_fk``** to ``sales_customer_groups``
27	  (nullable — a customer need not belong to a group). Contrast finance/inventory ids, which when
28	  referenced cross-module are opaque; the group is sales-owned so it is a real composite FK.
29	
30	Both tables follow the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop: ``tenant_unique()`` on every table a
31	child references, ``tenant_fk()`` composites for every INTRA-module cross-row link. Enum-valued
32	columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value (the core/finance/inventory/
33	procurement convention, no ``sa.Enum``); the service maps to/from the constants classes.
34	"""
35	
36	import uuid
37	
38	import sqlalchemy as sa
39	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
40	
41	from app.core.models import (
42	    AuditMixin,
43	    Base,
44	    TenantMixin,
45	    TimestampMixin,
46	    UuidPKMixin,
47	    tenant_fk,
48	    tenant_unique,
49	)
50	from app.core.money import MoneyType
51	from app.modules.sales.constants import (
52	    DEFAULT_CREDIT_LIMIT,
53	    DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS,
54	    CustomerStatus,
55	)
56	
57	
58	class CustomerGroup(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
59	    """A customer group — a lean grouping master pricing keys on (PLAN 7.1).
60	
61	    ``code`` is user-supplied and unique per tenant; ``name`` is the display label. The group
62	    carries NO pricing of its own: it is purely a key a ``Customer`` belongs to and a ``PriceList``
63	    can target (constants.py documents the master-table-over-free-string choice). Audited (D-010): a
64	    grouping that steers which prices a customer sees is master data worth tracking.
65	    ``tenant_unique`` so customers + price lists can composite-FK to it."""
66	
67	    __tablename__ = "sales_customer_groups"
68	    __table_args__ = (
69	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
70	            "tenant_id", "code", name="uq_sales_customer_groups_tenant_id_code"
71	        ),
72	        tenant_unique(),
73	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
74	    )

1	"""Sales' cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Sales sits above inventory and finance in the dependency order: the O2C documents in 7.2–7.4
4	(quote → order → delivery → invoice) and finance AR reporting read THIS file to resolve customer
5	state + prices synchronously; sales imports finance/queries + inventory/queries downward. Keep this
6	surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is the ONLY sales file other modules import.
7	
8	The central D-029 link: finance AR stores a customer on each invoice/receipt as an opaque
9	``partner_id`` (no FK). ``get_customer_for_partner`` resolves that ``partner_id`` back to a
10	``Customer`` so AR aging / reporting can render the customer's name and payment terms — the
11	``partner_id`` IS the ``Customer.id``, so it is a thin alias over ``get_customer`` named for the
12	reporting intent (the exact mirror of procurement's ``get_vendor_for_partner``).
13	
14	The PRICE RESOLVER is exposed here too: ``resolve_price`` is the public entry point 7.2's order
15	entry prices each line through, delegating to ``service/price_resolution.resolve_price`` (the
16	deterministic best-match picker, D-043). Putting it in queries.py keeps the rule that other modules
17	import only this file.
18	
19	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
20	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
21	"""
22	
23	import uuid
24	from datetime import date
25	from decimal import Decimal
26	
27	from sqlalchemy import select
28	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
29	
30	from app.modules.sales.constants import CustomerStatus
31	from app.modules.sales.models import Customer
32	from app.modules.sales.service.price_resolution import ResolvedPrice
33	from app.modules.sales.service.price_resolution import resolve_price as _resolve_price
34	
35	
36	async def get_customer(
37	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
38	) -> Customer | None:
39	    """The customer with ``customer_id`` in the tenant, or None. Lets another module read a
40	    customer's master fields (name, status, default currency, payment terms, credit limit) without
41	    importing sales models directly — the analogue of procurement's ``get_vendor``."""
42	    stmt = select(Customer).where(
43	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
44	    )
45	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
46	
47	
48	async def get_customer_for_partner(
49	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, partner_id: uuid.UUID
50	) -> Customer | None:
51	    """The customer an AR document's opaque ``partner_id`` refers to (D-029), or None. AR aging /
52	    reporting calls this to resolve an invoice's ``partner_id`` to a customer name + payment terms.
53	    The ``partner_id`` IS the ``Customer.id`` (finance stores it without an FK), so this is
54	    ``get_customer`` named for the reporting intent — kept as its own function so AR call sites read
55	    intent-first and the alias survives any future indirection (the vendor precedent)."""
56	    return await get_customer(session, tenant_id, partner_id)
57	
58	
59	async def customer_exists(
60	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
61	) -> bool:
62	    """Whether a customer with ``customer_id`` exists in the tenant. The cheap existence check a
63	    quote / order line uses to validate its customer_id (the sales analogue of inventory's
64	    ``item_exists``)."""
65	    stmt = select(Customer.id).where(
66	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
67	    )
68	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
69	
70	
71	async def customer_status(
72	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
73	) -> CustomerStatus | None:
74	    """The customer's lifecycle status (ACTIVE/BLOCKED/INACTIVE), or None if the customer does not
75	    exist. 7.2's order flow reads this to refuse a NEW order against a non-ACTIVE customer (the soft
76	    block, distinct from the credit-limit block)."""
77	    stmt = select(Customer.status).where(
78	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
79	    )
80	    value = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
81	    return CustomerStatus(value) if value is not None else None
82	
83	
84	async def customer_credit_limit(
85	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
86	) -> Decimal | None:
87	    """The customer's static credit limit = max outstanding AR (D-043), or None if the customer does
88	    not exist. 7.2's order confirmation reads this for the credit-limit block: 0 = cash-only (no
89	    open credit allowed), a positive value = the ceiling. Exposed so the order flow need not import
90	    sales models."""
91	    stmt = select(Customer.credit_limit).where(
92	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
93	    )
94	    value = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
95	    return Decimal(str(value)) if value is not None else None
96	
97	
98	async def customer_payment_terms_days(
99	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
100	) -> int | None:
101	    """The customer's net-days payment terms (e.g. 30 = NET30), or None if the customer does not
102	    exist. The order→invoice flow (7.4) reads this to default an invoice's due date (invoice_date +
103	    days), the same math AR uses today — exposed so the chain need not import sales models."""
104	    stmt = select(Customer.payment_terms_days).where(
105	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
106	    )
107	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
108	
109	
110	async def customer_default_currency(
111	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
112	) -> str | None:
113	    """The customer's default currency code (ISO alpha-3), or None if the customer does not exist.
114	    The quote/order flow (7.2) defaults a document's currency from this; exposed so the chain need
115	    not import sales models."""
116	    stmt = select(Customer.default_currency_code).where(
117	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
118	    )
119	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
120	
121	
122	async def resolve_price(
123	    session: AsyncSession,
124	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
125	    *,
126	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
127	    customer_id: uuid.UUID,
128	    on_date: date,
129	    quantity: Decimal,
130	    currency: str,
131	) -> ResolvedPrice:
132	    """The applicable base unit price for an item/customer/date/quantity/currency (PLAN 7.1, D-043).
133	
134	    The public entry point 7.2's order entry prices each line through. Delegates to the
135	    deterministic best-match resolver in ``service/price_resolution`` (documented there); returns a
136	    :class:`ResolvedPrice` whose ``matched`` is False when no ACTIVE price list applies. Bounded to
137	    two queries — no N+1. Exposed here so other modules import only ``sales/queries``."""
138	    return await _resolve_price(
139	        session,
140	        tenant_id,
141	        item_id=item_id,
142	        customer_id=customer_id,
143	        on_date=on_date,
144	        quantity=quantity,
145	        currency=currency,
146	    )

1	"""The condition-style price resolver (PLAN 7.1, D-043): resolve the applicable base unit price for
2	an item + customer + date + quantity + currency.
3	
4	This is the v1 pricing engine the s4hana-parity Sales section scopes to: price lists by
5	currency/customer-group/date-range with a base price per item — NOT the generalized access-sequence
6	engine. ``resolve_price`` is the single deterministic best-match picker; it is exposed to other
7	modules via ``sales/queries.resolve_price`` (7.2's order entry prices each line through it).
8	
9	**Deterministic resolution order (D-043).** Among the price lists that APPLY — i.e. all of:
10	
11	1. ``status == ACTIVE`` (INACTIVE lists are never priced from);
12	2. ``currency_code == currency`` (a list prices in exactly one currency);
13	3. ``valid_from <= on_date`` AND (``valid_to IS NULL`` OR ``valid_to >= on_date``) — the date is in
14	   the inclusive window;
15	4. the list is GENERAL (``customer_group_id IS NULL``) OR targets the customer's group
16	   (``customer_group_id == customer.customer_group_id``); a list targeting a DIFFERENT group, or
17	   any group when the customer has none, does not apply;
18	5. the list has a ``PriceListItem`` for ``item_id`` whose ``min_quantity <= quantity``;
19	
20	the winner is chosen by, in strict order:
21	
22	  a. **highest ``priority``** (the explicit tenant override; higher integer wins);
23	  b. then **most specific**: a GROUP-TARGETED list beats a GENERAL (null-group) list;
24	  c. then **latest ``valid_from``** (the most recently effective list wins — a newer campaign price
25	     supersedes an older one);
26	  d. then **price-list ``id``** as a final stable tiebreaker (so the result is fully deterministic
27	     even for two otherwise-identical lists — pathological, but the order must never depend on row
28	     order).
29	
30	If nothing applies, the resolver returns a "no match" result; 7.2's order entry then requires a
31	manual price or an override. NO discount is applied here — the price list yields the base price only
32	(discounts are a per-order-line concern in 7.2).
33	
34	**Boundedness (PERFORMANCE §6, no N+1).** Two queries total, regardless of how many lists exist:
35	ONE query fetches the small set of candidate ACTIVE lists matching currency+date+group (index-served
36	by ``ix_sales_price_lists_resolver``); ONE query fetches, for those candidate lists, the
37	``PriceListItem`` rows for this item meeting ``min_quantity`` (index-served by
38	``ix_sales_price_list_items_tenant_id_item_id``). The winner is then picked in Python over that
39	small joined set — no per-list round trip.
40	"""
41	
42	import uuid
43	from dataclasses import dataclass
44	from datetime import date
45	from decimal import Decimal
46	
47	from sqlalchemy import select
48	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
49	
50	from app.modules.sales.constants import PriceListStatus
51	from app.modules.sales.models import Customer, PriceList, PriceListItem
52	
53	
54	@dataclass(frozen=True)
55	class ResolvedPrice:
56	    """The outcome of ``resolve_price`` (D-043). ``matched`` False means no ACTIVE price list
57	    applied
58	    (all price fields None). When matched, ``unit_price`` is the base price in ``currency_code`` and
59	    ``price_list_id`` / ``price_list_code`` name the winning list. No discount is applied (base
60	    price
61	    only)."""
62	
63	    matched: bool
64	    unit_price: Decimal | None = None
65	    price_list_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
66	    price_list_code: str | None = None
67	    currency_code: str | None = None
68	
69	
70	_NO_MATCH = ResolvedPrice(matched=False)
71	
72	
73	async def resolve_price(
74	    session: AsyncSession,
75	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
76	    *,
77	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
78	    customer_id: uuid.UUID,
79	    on_date: date,
80	    quantity: Decimal,
81	    currency: str,
82	) -> ResolvedPrice:
83	    """Resolve the applicable base unit price for an item/customer/date/quantity/currency (D-043).
84	
85	    Returns a :class:`ResolvedPrice`; ``matched`` is False (all price fields None) when no ACTIVE
86	    price list applies. The deterministic best-match order is documented at the top of this module.
87	    Bounded to two queries (the candidate lists, then their items for this item) — no N+1.
88	    """
89	    customer = (
90	        await session.execute(
91	            select(Customer.customer_group_id).where(
92	                Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
93	            )
94	        )
95	    ).first()
96	    if customer is None:
97	        # An unknown customer cannot have a resolved price — the caller (7.2) validates the customer
98	        # exists before pricing, so this is a defensive no-match rather than an error path.
99	        return _NO_MATCH
100	    customer_group_id = customer[0]
101	
102	    # Query 1: the candidate ACTIVE lists matching currency + date window + (general OR this
103	    # customer's group). A list targeting a different group is excluded in SQL; a list targeting
104	    # ANY group is excluded when the customer has none (the `is_(None)` arm only).
105	    group_match = PriceList.customer_group_id.is_(None)
106	    if customer_group_id is not None:
107	        group_match = group_match | (PriceList.customer_group_id == customer_group_id)
108	    candidate_stmt = select(PriceList).where(
109	        PriceList.tenant_id == tenant_id,
110	        PriceList.status == PriceListStatus.ACTIVE.value,
111	        PriceList.currency_code == currency,
112	        PriceList.valid_from <= on_date,
113	        (PriceList.valid_to.is_(None)) | (PriceList.valid_to >= on_date),
114	        group_match,
115	    )
116	    candidates = list((await session.execute(candidate_stmt)).scalars().all())
117	    if not candidates:
118	        return _NO_MATCH
119	
120	    # Query 2: the price rows for THIS item on the candidate lists that meet the quantity floor.
121	    candidate_ids = [pl.id for pl in candidates]
122	    item_stmt = select(PriceListItem).where(
123	        PriceListItem.tenant_id == tenant_id,
124	        PriceListItem.item_id == item_id,
125	        PriceListItem.price_list_id.in_(candidate_ids),
126	        PriceListItem.min_quantity <= quantity,
127	    )
128	    item_rows = list((await session.execute(item_stmt)).scalars().all())
129	    if not item_rows:
130	        return _NO_MATCH
131	
132	    # Join the price rows to their lists in Python (the candidate set is small) and pick the winner
133	    # by the D-043 sort key: priority desc, specificity (group-targeted > general) desc, valid_from
134	    # desc, then list id as the final stable tiebreaker.
135	    lists_by_id = {pl.id: pl for pl in candidates}
136	
137	    def sort_key(row: PriceListItem) -> tuple[int, int, date, str]:
138	        pl = lists_by_id[row.price_list_id]
139	        is_group_targeted = 1 if pl.customer_group_id is not None else 0
140	        return (pl.priority, is_group_targeted, pl.valid_from, str(pl.id))
141	
142	    winner_row = max(item_rows, key=sort_key)
143	    winner_list = lists_by_id[winner_row.price_list_id]
144	    return ResolvedPrice(
145	        matched=True,
146	        unit_price=Decimal(str(winner_row.unit_price)),
147	        price_list_id=winner_list.id,
148	        price_list_code=winner_list.code,
149	        currency_code=winner_list.currency_code,
150	    )
